translatedData.body:
For large holders, self-custody is the core of asset security.

An exchange may compensate you once, twice, or even many times.

But the moment there is a single hack that causes losses exceeding what the platform can cover, it becomes a sea of corpses and blood.

So what truly matters is never “how much the exchange promises to pay,” but rather not exposing all assets to a single point of failure.

Large assets should be distributed across multiple cold wallets; for day-to-day use, reconfigure only a small amount of hot wallets. The exchange should hold only the necessary trading funds.

Store in layers: cold wallets, hot wallets, and exchanges.

An exchange’s advantage is convenience, but its drawback is concentration.

The more massive assets are concentrated, the more easily they become an attack target.

What big holders should manage isn’t just return rates, but their own probability of survival.
